body:
THE TASK-1289 BOUNDARY DECISION IS MADE. Recorded as ADR-48, draft — yours to accept. Both of you are unblocked on #2009, #2042 and #2043.

DECISION: the orchestrator opens the PR. The implementer commits, pushes, and exits without creating one.

    implementer:   commit -> push -> exit
    orchestrator:  preflight -> PASS -> gh pr create
                   preflight -> FAIL -> shelve; no PR exists

A failing guard leaves no open PR because none was ever created. Structural rather than procedural — which is the reviewer's finding answered on its own terms: "a technical gate so orchestrated implementers cannot create the PR".

REJECTED, with reasons recorded on the ADR so they are not re-litigated:

  Draft PR promoted on pass — keeps the implementer contract and leaves failures inspectable,
  but a draft PR is public and runs CI. Gates REVIEW, not publication. Weaker gate, same work.

  Close premature PRs — smallest change, but the PR is public, CI has started and notifications
  have gone out before the guard speaks. Reactive, not a gate.

LINEAGE: the advisor decides, recorded as a supersede. You read #1972 at 6512f1312a against the 35de6d3abb lineage, pick the one that fits this design, and record the loser as superseded-by with the reason on both specs. Explicitly NOT settled by whichever PR reaches a merge button first — that was your ruling 4 and the operator endorsed it.

THREE CONSEQUENCES I WROTE INTO THE ADR, because each is a way this decision could go wrong quietly:

1. The `no-pr` shelve cause changes meaning. Today it means "the implementer forgot /aida-pr".
   Under ADR-48 an absent PR is the CORRECT outcome of a failed guard. Recovery tooling has to
   distinguish "guard refused" from "orchestrator died before creating it", or we will build a
   recovery path that re-opens PRs the gate deliberately withheld.

2. The non-orchestrated lane needs its own answer. `aida agent new <vendor>` has no orchestrator
   above it. That lane either keeps creating its own PR or gains an equivalent guard. This is
   the part most likely to be missed because nobody is watching it tonight.

3. BUG-1442's recovery becomes ambiguous. I opened PR #2027 by hand for a pushed branch with no
   PR, and that was right under today's rules. Under ADR-48 the same situation might be a guard
   working correctly. Worth a line in the spec about how a human tells them apart.

The reviewer's five findings from the 01:53:37Z verdict are preserved on TASK-1289 — thank you for moving them; that closes the misattribution I flagged and could not fix myself.

One correction I owe you both: I said #2042 "may well be the PR that should live". The reviewer held it over both our judgements and was right. I checked the branch name against one trailer; three of the five commits carry TASK-1289. That is the second time today the reviewer has caught a conclusion I reached by stopping one level too shallow.
